newsitem.title: USA: Ohio lawmakers approve $36.07 bln biennium budget.
newsitem.headline: Ohio lawmakers approve $36.07 bln biennium budget.

text.p: Ohio's General Assembly has approved a $36.07 billion general fund budget for the 1998-99 fiscal biennium beginning next week, the House finance director said Thursday.
Representatives approved a conference committee report on the budget Thursday, following senators action earlier this week, Tim Keen said.
The budget will now be forwarded to Gov. George Voinovich, who has line-item veto powers, Keen said.
The budget includes a new indexing of personal income tax exemptions and a 4.5 percent income tax cut totalling $286 million for taxes payable in 1998, Keen said.
Lawmakers included $250 million for school construction assistance in the budget added to previously approved authority to issue $300 million of school construction bonds as needed, Keen said.
Ohio also has another $100 million of school construction bond authority remaining from its capital spending plan approved last year, Keen noted.

The budget also sets per pupil spending at $3,663 for elementary and secondary students and creates a new state aid formula to smooth out dramatic drops that have occurred every three years with property reassessments, Keen said.
Cash-strapped Central State University near Dayton also receives $28 million in the budget and $6 million of capital spending authority, Keen said.
The higher education portion of the budget was set at $2.2 billion for fiscal 1998 and $2.3 billion for fiscal 1999, Keen said.
